lead_decisions.on: the open question at efc1fe96: refuse the whole open on an invalid entry, or refuse on read
lead_decisions.decision: Refuse on read, as multicam does. One bad settings or preset entry must not lock the whole file out of opening. A package with an invalid entry opens; reading it gives the typed refusal; a commit that would use it is refused and leaves the document and entry untouched; save keeps it byte-for-byte unless a successful commit replaces it; never dropped silently; report it through the existing open-time notes if they fit, and add no new mechanism if they do not.

notes.loss_notes_fit: LossReason::Opaque fits and is used, so no new mechanism was added. Its docs say "preserved, not semantically imported", and LossNote says "preserved-opaque, not semantically imported (STU-IO-004/005)", which is exactly an entry kept verbatim that the session cannot use. The note names the entry (studio/<token>.<sha256>). For a repeated token each entry is noted. An entry already noted Unlisted keeps that note. A note goes when the entry is replaced by a commit or a set. Notes stay as of open: an entry the document later comes to validate keeps its note until the session closes.

declared_readings: Invalid entry forms that open and refuse on read: bytes that are not JSON, JSON that fails the Folio types or bounds, records that do not validate against the document, bytes past the Folio input budget, and two well-formed entries of one token (DuplicateIdentity, neither chosen).

A name whose digest is not the body's (or has no digest) is not a document entry of the token. It stays an ordinary opaque entry with its existing loss note, as before this lane, is saved verbatim, and the typed read answers None. A commit can then store a new entry beside it.

A commit that would use an invalid entry: all three commands read the settings entry; save and apply read the preset entry, even for a shipped preset, because a stored preset could shadow it; set does not read presets, so a bad preset entry does not stop it. Those answer folio_rejected or budget_exceeded. A step that quotes a held entry that does not parse, or a repeated token, answers value_conflict, multicam's rule, including a quote of None. A step that keeps quoted invalid records unchanged while anything else changes answers folio_rejected.

What does not use it commits and leaves its bytes alone: a timeline step, a multicam step, a records step on the other entry. The commit and resync guards protect a valid settings entry only; an entry already invalid does not hold them up.

Replacing an invalid entry: a step that quotes parsable invalid records and writes valid ones or None commits. Bytes that do not parse, and a repeated token, cannot be quoted, so an explicit set_sequence_settings_records / set_sequence_presets (valid records or None) is the way out of them. That is explicit, not a silent drop, and goes beyond the lead's wording of a successful commit; flagged at 0f3cc50d with no objection recorded yet.

The undo of a commit that replaced an invalid entry is refused folio_rejected, because it would write invalid records back; the repair stands (a_successful_commit_replaces_a_parsable_invalid_entry). This is the one step in the lane without a working inverse.

Accepted by the lead: a commit that changes the frame rate of a sequence with a valid settings entry without changing the entry is refused folio_rejected, because the entry's frame_rate must equal the sequence's. A stale multicam entry after a timeline step stays allowed, as before. A sequence without an entry is unaffected. The records step can change the rate and the entry together.

Accepted by the lead: the _as forms of the new step refuse actor_mismatch (the context's actor is not the session's), command_mismatch and a stale base revision. submit_multicam_as checks none of these. Grants and receipts belong to the session's actor and a context grants nothing, so a mismatch is refused rather than attributed.

The records step reuses SequenceEdit, so a sequence and its entry can be inserted or removed in one revision. A Remove there is also checked against the multicam records so this new path does not bypass multicam's own refusal. A Replace is not, as a timeline step is not.

save_from_sequence and apply look presets up in the stored set plus the shipped library, a stored preset shadowing a shipped one of the same id. Only stored presets are written, so a save does not copy the 391 shipped rows into the document. Applied::sequence_settings_report.presets counts stored presets, not the library Folio saw.

A keyed command's binding covers the command, its context's command id and correlation, and the expected revision, not the entries: a retry after commit must replay, and the commit itself changes the entries. A keyed step's binding covers its quoted records. A commit authority receives only the successor document in both cases, as multicam.
Direct set of these two tokens must parse and validate, and is refused reconciliation_required while a commit is pending; removing an entry stays possible so a diverged key can still be resynced.
sequences_without_settings sends no Observe frame, as the other typed reads do not.

notes.undo_after_reopen: Multicam does it: tests/multicam_commit.rs committed_multicam_step_survives_save_and_reopen undoes on the reopened document with an inverse taken before the save. History itself is not persisted. So it was in scope here and is proven the same way, by settings_library_and_mode_survive_save_and_reopen_through_the_session. An undo with no inverse held by the caller is not possible after a reopen, for multicam or here.
notes.hostile_input: Crate-level V4-01 deny applies to the new modules. V4-02: Folio's preflight bounds bytes and depth before any parse, then counts lists; a body the step would store is parsed back through the same check a read uses, so one over the input budget is refused budget_exceeded at commit. risks.risk: Receipts hold each keyed step's inverse, so a library-sized step keeps two copies of the library per held receipt: at most 1024 receipts with bodies of at most the 1 MiB input budget, about 2 GiB in the worst case. Multicam and timeline receipts have the same shape with sequence values.
risks.mitigation: None added; acknowledged receipts evict. A preset add/remove delta in the step would shrink it if this ever shows up.

risks.risk: A caller that does not read Session::loss and only sees None or a refused command may not know a file holds a bad entry. The read and the commands do say so; None is only answered for an absent or misnamed entry.
risks.mitigation: The note is at open and the harness op record already carries the loss-note count.
